passed_facts.quote: PRIMARY: 'when a batch aborts halfway, self.last_report should still read whatever the last good run left...accumulating into locals and constructing the EncodingReport at the end, then assigning it to the attribute once, on the success path after the loop has finished. If the loop raises, no write ever happens and the previous value survives by construction' (g9.r2.l19, mail, lines 1336-1339, step 17). This is the mechanism the agent implemented verbatim: format_batch accumulates dropped_indices/windowed/supervised_tokens as locals inside the loop and assigns self.last_report exactly once, after the loop — so ANY exception that escapes the inner `except ExampleTooLongError` clause (i.e. InvalidRoleSequenceError from validate_role_sequence, or TokenizerCapabilityError) aborts before that single assignment and last_report keeps its prior value. SECONDARY: the narrow catch shape itself ('except ExampleTooLongError:') traces to the r1.h1/rev1 exchange establishing that format_batch specifically skips-and-continues on ExampleTooLongError ('skip stays. format_batch skips it and carrys on', line 1291) — nowhere does the agent's Analysis/Plan text discuss role-sequence or tokenizer-capability errors as a distinct drop-vs-raise question. The one remark that speaks to that question directly, g9.r2.h-role-row (the herring: 'Length and role sequence are row problems...counted and skipped'), WAS seen (line 1350, step 17, inside the same say23 email) but is never mentioned, endorsed, or acted on anywhere in the transcript; the agent's very next Analysis (line 1412) talks only about the atomicity requirement and the too-long error message. The four remarks that would have reversed the herring explicitly (g9.r2.l16, l17, say24, rev3) never surfaced in this run at all (0 mechanical hits, confirmed absent by direct grep). So the agent got this fact right by construction — the accumulate-then-assign-once pattern from l19, combined with a narrow except clause modeled on r1's ExampleTooLongError-only skip — not by reading and reasoning about the herring or its reversal. Confirmed deliberate (not lucky) by its own regression test: `with pytest.raises(InvalidRoleSequenceError): formatter.format_batch([good, policy_example(["user"])])` followed by `assert formatter.last_report is previous` (test_policy_reports_are_frozen_and_atomic) explicitly locks in exactly this behavior. No equivalent test exercises TokenizerCapabilityError THROUGH format_batch (only through to_tinker_datum directly), so that half is correct by the same except-clause construction but was not separately verified by the agent.

search_strategy: Ticket-driven, then broad-then-narrow. Early steps (1-9) pulled Mattermost via a bulk channel-history dump to /tmp/channels.txt and IMAP mail to /tmp/mail.txt, then grepped both with a fixed keyword list ('encoding|supervised|window|formatter|length cap', later 'pair|utf-8|serialize|...'). A parallel /tmp/chat-search.json (Mattermost search API) was parsed with inline python3 one-liners that print only the first ~2200 chars of each matched post body, which is why several chat herrings/reversals surfaced as isolated one-line fragments rather than full exchanges (e.g. g9.r2.g9-tuple-return-1/2 herrings — only their opening questions were ever in view). Wiki access was via curl to the BookStack REST API and head -c on saved page dumps (/tmp/page137.txt, /tmp/page144.txt etc.) — 9 of the 15 wiki-comment clues were never fetched at all, all falling on pages the agent never opened (no comment-body coverage gap beyond the pages it didn't visit). No crashed helper scripts; the main friction was heredoc/foreground wedging flagged repeatedly by the horizon watchdog, costing turns but not information. Mail was read via grep over a pre-dumped /tmp/mail.txt rather than live IMAP SEARCH/FETCH calls, but coverage looks equivalent to a full mailbox scan (13/13 mail clues that mattered for fact coverage were found; only 2 mail-only remarks, l-fail-1's chat duplicate aside, were missed and both were redundant with other found remarks carrying the same fact).
end_reason: Completed normally: implemented and pushed to main as 92c8a9a; all 113 finetune tests pass; CI run 14 green; deployed encoding.py matches main (final Analysis, transcript line 3648).
notable: Line 1126 (step 10): the h1 herring text is reworded by the world ('that was the call yes. any nonzero window_start...') rather than matching the answer key's dialogue framing verbatim, though the load-bearing sentence ('an example we had to cut isnt really an example anymore, its an artifact') is identical — judged as seen per reader_instructions.

The g9.r2.h-role-row herring and the true clue g9.r2.say23 are the SAME email (Dario's 2025-05-28 11:06 reply) — the herring is a sub-quote of the message that also carries the correct scope fact. The agent saw both halves in one read and simply never engaged with the role-sequence-as-drop half.

g9.r2.failure_behavior was scored correctly without ever seeing any of the four remarks (l16, l17, say24, rev3) that state or reverse the InvalidRoleSequenceError/TokenizerCapabilityError-propagate rule directly. The pass is explained entirely by g9.r2.l19 (atomic accumulate-then-assign-once) plus the narrow except-ExampleTooLongError shape inherited from r1's refusal thread — a case where two correct but not-directly-on-point clues compose into the right answer.

9 of 15 wiki-comment clues were never fetched (l11, l8(r2), l-fw-2, l-scope-3, l-rule-4, say24(r2), l17, rev3, l5(r2), say24(r1)) — consistent with the answer key's warning that BookStack search does not index comments; every miss is on a page the agent's page-fetch list simply never included, not a comment the agent saw the body of but skipped.

The chat-search JSON dump (step 10) truncates each matched post to ~2200 characters and appears to print isolated single messages rather than full threads, which is why both tuple-return herrings were only ever seen as their opening question, never their resolving answer — the resolving answers reached the agent later, correctly, via the mail/history grep at step 13.
